text: Why is a fixed absolute tolerance such as 1e-6 unreliable?
choices: It fails only for negative numbers
It is meaningless without knowing the magnitude: at 10^-9 everything passes, at 10^16 nothing does
Tolerances must always be powers of two
It is too small for any practical use
explanation: Near 10^16 the gap between adjacent doubles is 2.0, so values as close as the format allows differ by more than 1e-6 and the test always says 'different'. Near 10^-9 every pair is within 1e-6 and it always says 'equal'. Scaling the tolerance to the larger operand makes the test mean the same thing at every scale.
